assistant|yoga_app_recommendation: Down Dog: wide range of classes, levels and styles (Hatha, Vinyasa, Restorative), various teachers; free trial then subscription
YogaGlo: over 4,000 classes, various styles/levels/focuses, filterable by teacher, level or focus; free trial then subscription
Alo Moves: vast library of yoga, Pilates and meditation classes with well-known teachers; free trial then subscription
Pocket Yoga: pose library, classes and customizable practices; one-time purchase, no subscription
Yoga Studio: pose library, classes and customizable practices, user-friendly; one-time purchase, no subscription
Daily Yoga: variety of classes incl. Hatha, Vinyasa, Restorative plus meditation and Pilates; free with in-app purchases
Omstars: yoga, Pilates and meditation classes with different teachers and styles; free trial then subscription
Gaia: yoga and meditation app with classes, workshops and lectures focused on spiritual growth; free trial then subscription
self|fitness_tracker: Has been using a Fitbit Charge 3 for 6 months; it helps stay on track with daily steps (on 2022-12-18)
Has been using a Fitbit Charge 3 for 9 months
assistant|step_goal_motivation_tip: Treat daily step goal as a non-negotiable appointment; set a reminder on Fitbit or phone
On low-motivation days start small with 5,000-7,000 steps instead of the usual 10,000
Build a habit with a short 10-15 minute walk after breakfast or lunch, even on Sundays
Find an accountability buddy among friends or family to hold each other to step goals
Mix up the routine with a bike ride, backyard laps or light stretching at home
Set small rewards for reaching the daily step goal (favorite snack, bath, fun activity)
Use the Fitbit app to track progress and see closeness to the goal as a motivator
Make walks enjoyable with music, podcasts or audiobooks
Get fresh air and natural light with even a short walk around the block
Be kind to yourself on off days; focus on getting moving rather than hitting the exact goal

assistant|sleep_tip_schedule: Go to bed and wake up at the same time every day; aim for 7-9 hours of sleep
assistant|sleep_tip_environment: Bedroom should be dark, quiet, and cool (around 60-67°F) with comfortable mattress and pillows
assistant|sleep_tip_wind_down: Wind down with calming activity like reading, meditation, or warm bath; avoid screens at least an hour before bed
assistant|sleep_tip_stimulants: Avoid caffeine 4-6 hours before bed and limit alcohol; nicotine can disrupt sleep patterns
assistant|sleep_tip_naps: Keep naps short (20-30 minutes) and avoid napping close to bedtime
assistant|sleep_tip_sunlight: Get morning sunlight exposure to help regulate circadian rhythms
assistant|sleep_tip_diary: Consider keeping a sleep diary to track sleep patterns and identify areas for adjustment
assistant|screen_replacement_tip: Replace screen time with relaxing activity like reading, calming music, or gentle stretches
assistant|blue_light_filter_tip: Use blue light filtering glasses or apps like f.lux or Twilight to reduce blue light effects
assistant|calming_content_tip: Choose calming TV content like nature documentaries, cooking shows, or gentle comedies
assistant|fitbit_sleep_tracking_tip: Fitbit Charge 3 has sleep tracking features showing duration, sleep stages, and sleep quality
assistant|roller_tip_pressure: Start with light pressure when using massage roller and gradually increase as needed
assistant|roller_tip_technique: Use long, slow strokes with massage roller; target trigger points and roll in multiple directions
assistant|roller_tip_breathing: Breathe deeply while using massage roller: inhale through nose, exhale through mouth
assistant|snack_recommendation: Recommended snacks: trail mix, fresh fruit, energy balls, hard-boiled eggs, Greek yogurt, veggie sticks with hummus, protein smoothie, apple slices with almond butter, edamame, dark chocolate (70%+ cocoa)
